newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Data confirms weaker NZ economy in Sept qtr - BTNZ.
newsitem.headline: Data confirms weaker NZ economy in Sept qtr - BTNZ.

text.p: New Zealand retail sales and unemployment figures released on Thursday confirmed the view that the pace of the economy was subdued in the September quarter, Bankers Trust New Zealand economists said.
"Combined with Tuesday's CPI, the data is positive for the fixed interest market and negative for the currency," BTNZ said.
Monthly retail sales fell a seasonally-adjusted 0.6 percent in August, against BTNZ's expectations of a 1.5 percent fall.
Excluding automotive storetypes, retail sales were unchanged on July. In the three months to August, retail sales fell one percent compared to the previous quarter.
"Thus the retail sector is subdued, despite the impact of the tax cuts," BTNZ said.
Earlier, Employment Minister Wyatt Creech said the number of registered unemployed New Zealanders fell 0.1 percent to 154,133 in September, from 154,327 in August.
BTNZ said a small fall in September was the usual seasonal pattern.
"More importantly, registered unemployment was 3.5 percent higher than the same month last year. This is an acceleration from the annual rate of increase recorded in August (+2.5 percent)," it said.
BTNZ said job ads were also falling, which pointed to a weak September quarter for employment.
"We think employment will be flat to down slightly over the quarter. This would represent a sharp break from the trend of strong increases in employment," it said.

September quarter Household Labour Force Survey data, the official measure of unemployment, is due from Statistics New Zealand on November 8. June quarter data showed an unemployment rate of 6.1 percent.
